observations: Domain label (cognitive/visual attention) mismatches the actual content: DNA/RNA foundation models and geometric ('3D') attention-bias ML experiments. The dominant flag class is internal effect sizes, F1s, deltas, and pre-registered thresholds inside interpretation/pre-reg docs whose producing task (tNNN) is named in the doc title or body — the lint ignores title/frontmatter task tokens and paper-summary filenames as provenance, driving a very high false-positive rate (~36/40 traceable). Standard statistical conventions (alpha=0.05/0.10, 80% power, t-critical values) and pre-reg decision cutoffs also fire noisily. Truly-orphaned cases are rare and low-value: planned-N guesses, hardware IDs, loose author estimates. Redesign: treat tNNN title/frontmatter tokens and paper-doc identity as valid anchors, whitelist stat conventions and identifiers, and reserve flags for handwavy/planned estimates lacking any task or paper link.
